claim: Through the shipctl command line, a shipment that already has a label can still have its delivery address changed.
why: Every shipctl route to the address of a labelled shipment fails, each for a different reason: address refuses it outright, edit refuses address and postcode as LOCKED_WHEN_LABELLED and puts any other key such as delivery_address into extra, relabel reprints the stored address, and amend skips labelled rows in amend.apply_row. The obvious check is the documented bulk path: amend prints 'imported ...: 1 row(s)' and exits 0 for a labelled shipment, and edit --set delivery_address=... prints 'set'. Only show afterwards, or reading amend.py, reveals that the address did not change.

root.claim: Some shipctl command changes the delivery address of a labelled shipment

atoms.evidence: python3 shipctl.py address S-1001 '5 Mill Lane' 4401 -> error: S-1001 is labelled; the address on the label cannot change
amend prints 'imported fix.csv: 1 row(s)' but apply_row appends labelled shipments to result.skipped; show S-1001 still says 3 Mill Lane.
edit --set address=... is refused (LOCKED_WHEN_LABELLED); edit --set delivery_address=... only adds an extra field, the address stays 3 Mill Lane.
labels.reprint takes only a service and reprints the stored address.
